title: Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moiré Superlattices
abstract: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moiré superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoiré CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moiré length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.
summary: This work explores Charge Density Wave formation in coupled quantum chains, extending the model to Moiré superlattices. It demonstrates that interchain coupling and lattice mismatch act as critical control parameters, stabilizing various CDW phases. These phases host localized, symmetry-protected in-gap electronic states whose properties are dictated by the underlying moiré periodicity.
main_problem: The study investigates Charge Density Waves (CDWs) and the nature of localized in-gap electronic states arising from the interplay between electron-phonon coupling and lattice distortions in coupled chains.
main_result: The system exhibits a sequence of CDW phases (e.g., staggered-dimer, trimer) whose structure is tunable by interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch, leading to localized states in supermoiré superlattices.
method: The analysis employs theoretical modeling using the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Hamiltonian, solved via Monte Carlo simulations and electronic structure diagonalization to map out phase diagrams and band structures.
model_or_system: The model consists of coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains, analyzed in both lattice-matched and lattice-mismatched Moiré superlattice geometries. The Hamiltonian includes terms for intrachain distortion and interchain hopping.
key_observables: CDW phases (staggered-dimer, trimer), topological invariants (inversion invariant, winding number), energy gap size, and the spatial localization of in-gap electronic states.
important_parameters: Interchain tunneling ($t_{\perp}$), electron-phonon coupling ($\alpha$), and the lattice mismatch parameter ($\lambda_m$) which defines the Moiré length scale.
main_assumptions: Phonons are treated as classical variables, and the interchain tunneling decay is modeled exponentially based on the displacement field.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing CDW stability vs. coupling parameters, band structures revealing gap opening, and real-space probability densities confirming the localization of in-gap states within the supermoiré unit cell.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the CDW phases in simple coupled chains, then extends the analysis to the more complex, tunable regime of Moiré superlattices, detailing how lattice mismatch reconstructs the CDW order and dictates the nature of the localized electronic states.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between structural periodicity (Moiré superlattice) and the emergence of topologically protected, localized electronic states via CDW formation is highly relevant to understanding correlated electron physics in engineered quantum materials.
